figures_correct.reason: Both use the same correct figures, which I recomputed from the data: ARR $10.9M, NRR 96.4%, GRR 89.3%, change failure 7.7% (4 of 52 deploys), lead time 38h, R&D share 40.8%, eval pass rate 86% and seat use 75%; Y's slide 06 count of '4 customers, 7 requests' is also correct once R-999, from Q2, is left out.

no_invented_numbers.reason: Neither states a figure the data does not support; the only projection is slide 11's 'Activation: 5 more periods', which both label as a rough guide and not a commitment.

speed_with_quality.reason: X's slide 09 and 09b headlines say releases rose from 3 to 4 'but' change failure rose from 5.1% to 7.7%, outside its healthy range, and that review time rose from 9h to 13h; X's slide 08 headline also names the release checklist's wrong-way move. Y only puts the speed and failure figures side by side, and its slide 08 headline says '4 have moved' without the regression.

gaps_shown.reason: Both flag the same gaps with owners: the $10.3M revenue against $10.9M ARR mismatch (L18), Platform & security on slide 10, and AI gross margin on slide 12, both owned by the VP Engineering and due in Q4.

board_cut_usable.reason: Y gives a rendered 8-slide board cut that leads with the outcomes and the pricing-pilot ask on slide 18, although it still carries the internal 'Check before the board sees this' box on slide 05. X gives no board cut, only a note that it is awaiting sign-off.

overall.reason: The figures and gaps are the same in both, and X frames speed against quality more honestly in its slide 08 and 09 headlines. But X gives the CPO nothing to send to the board, while Y's board cut can be sent once the revenue/ARR check on slide 05 is resolved and that box is removed.
